q: The pitch of a note is determined by its _____.
e: Pitch is how high the note sounds, and frequency sets it. Raise frequency and pitch rises. Pitch is frequency; amplitude is loudness.

q: The greater the frequency of a sound wave, the _____ is the pitch.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Stiffer media generally carry it faster. Amplitude changes loudness, not high-or-low character.

q: The loudness of a note depends upon the _____ of the wave that produces it.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Density-pressure-temperature sets speed, not frequency.

q: The greater the amplitude, the louder the note, because more _____ is used to produce a larger amplitude.
e: greater and amplitude have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of greater would describe a different law. Radiation from an opaque solid is not scored as a mass phenomenon.

q: Quality or timbre of a sound is the characteristic which distinguishes two sounds of the same loudness and same pitch but emitted by two different _____.
e: Loudness is the ear's sensation of a sound. It usually grows with intensity, which itself grows with amplitude squared. Two listeners can disagree, so loudness is subjective. Timbre, or quality, lets you tell instruments apart at the same pitch and loudness.

q: The timbre of a sound depends on its waveform, which varies with the number of _____ or harmonics.
e: Timbre, or quality, lets you tell instruments apart at the same pitch and loudness. Overtones and waveform carry that colour. A violin sounds richer because it has more overtones. Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium.

q: The intensity of sound at a place is the energy transmitted per second per unit area held normally to the direction of _____.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Stiffer media generally carry it faster. Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2.

q: Loudness is a sensation and hence, unlike intensity, it is _____ and depends on the observer.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself. In Doppler formulas, fo is what the observer hears and vo is the observer's speed.

q: For a particular volume of sound, normally the greater the intensity, the _____ the loudness of the sound is.
e: Sound intensity is power per unit area, in W m^-2. Level in decibels is 10 log10 of I over I_0, with I_0 = 10^-12 W m^-2. Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, not to amplitude itself. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum.

q: Notes of the same pitch played upon different musical instruments are distinguished from each other by their quality, which is also called _____.
e: Timbre, or quality, lets you tell instruments apart at the same pitch and loudness. Overtones and waveform carry that colour. A violin sounds richer because it has more overtones. Raise frequency and pitch rises.

q: The notes produced by a violin are richer than others because it has more _____.
e: notes and produced have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of notes would describe a different law. Notes produced by a violin are richer cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.
